name: Independent review-derived zebrafish micro/nanoplastics–PFAS retrieval benchmark

scope.exposures: co-exposure to microplastics and/or nanoplastics plus at least one PFAS; other co-contaminants permitted and flagged
exclude: other species without a zebrafish experiment

method.candidate_generation: Review discovery through internet queries, followed by review body/HTML/JATS and/or publisher-deposited Crossref reference-list screening; original abstracts checked after references supplied candidate identities.
method.stopping_rule: Sources found through broad review discovery and their available reference lists were screened; no numeric target and no claim of saturation.
not_read: new topic-search results produced by lead agent
method.independence_from_topic_retrieval: The benchmark collector received only scope and a later freeze timestamp/hash; it never received or inspected the lead topic-retrieval results. Candidate generation did not use that output.
blinding_caveats: Review-discovery search results incidentally included primary papers. Those results were not themselves sufficient for benchmark inclusion; explicit review/reference-list provenance was subsequently required.

Before the lead requested concealment, one progress message named Yang 2020 and its F-53B subject. Therefore this workflow is not strict researcher blinding, even though source construction remained independent.
Review/source selection was adaptive and was not preregistered. Only the separate lead topic-search plan was reported frozen.

lead_freeze_communication.note: Timestamp/hash were received as a message; this collector did not open the plan file.

method.copyright: Only bibliographic metadata and short paraphrases retained; no full review or abstract text copied into these deliverables.
method.logging: Exact web queries/open/find arguments and returned result URLs retained. Returned search-result URLs do not mean each result was separately opened. Python network endpoints and failures retained. Per-request timestamps were not captured; date and logical batch order are recorded, with some batches concurrent.

limitations: This is a five-paper review-derived find-back set, not the denominator of all eligible research in the field; recall against it must be labelled benchmark recall only.
The original-paper years in this set are 2018, 2020 and 2024. Reviews have citation and search cut-off lag; absence of 2025–2026 experiments here does not show their absence from the field.

Publisher 403/429 responses, PMC browser challenges and inaccessible review supplements limited full-text coverage. Crossref reference lists are used explicitly as reference-list evidence, not as proof of full-text access.

Review-level title/reference screening may miss studies whose titles omit species or exposure details. A broadly titled mixed-contaminant study was checked and included, but this does not make all reference screening exhaustive.
Two deposited DOI strings in the R11 reference list remained 404 after retry. They were not silently corrected or counted as read.
B05 includes several contaminant classes alongside PFAS; it satisfies exposure scope but cannot establish a plastic–PFAS binary-specific toxicity effect.
No pooled toxicity interpretation, risk ranking or effect-size meta-analysis was performed.

recall_evaluation.instruction: Lead may compare a frozen topic-retrieval result with these DOI/PMID identifiers only after its retrieval is complete. Keep benchmark false negatives distinct from evidence that the whole-field search is complete.
